eggedal_molle.name: Molino de Eggedal
eggedal_molle.desc: Traducción al español: Historic mill in Eggedal that shows local grain milling, water power, rural technology and small-scale production. The place gives Sigdal a practical point of labour history.
eggedal_molle.popupDesc: Traducción al español: Eggedal Mill is a concrete place of labour history. Mills were necessary technical hubs in farming communities: they turned grain into flour, gathered people, required water power and local expertise, and often stood close to other small industries. In History Go, Eggedal Mill should be used to show everyday technology and economy, not only the large works and factories.

drammen_tollbod_havn.name: Drammen Customs House / Harbour Area
drammen_tollbod_havn.desc: Traducción al español: Customs-house and harbour environment in Drammen, linked to timber, shipping, customs revenues and the city’s role as a trading and export town by the Drammen River.
drammen_tollbod_havn.popupDesc: Traducción al español: Drammen grew through river, harbour, timber, trade and international shipping. The customs house and harbour area make this concrete: here goods were registered, taxed, loaded, exported and controlled. In History Go, the place should be used to show how the city was not only buildings and streets, but an economic system of forest, river, sawmills, ships, customs, workers, merchants and the world market.

kjerraten_i_asa.name: The Kjerrat at Åsa
kjerraten_i_asa.desc: Traducción al español: Historic timber-transport installation at Åsa, built to pull timber from Steinsfjorden up toward the Damtjern system. The kjerrat shows forest economy, engineering, water power and physical labour in the Ringerike landscape.
kjerraten_i_asa.popupDesc: Traducción al español: The Kjerrat at Åsa is one of Buskerud’s clearest technical-historical cultural monuments. The installation was built in the early 1800s to lift timber up from Steinsfjorden and onward into waterways that could carry it toward the markets. In History Go, the place should be used for timber history, landscape reading, engineering and the connection between forest resources and urban and industrial economy.

hassel_jernverk.name: Hassel Ironworks
hassel_jernverk.desc: Traducción al español: Former ironworks in Modum, with roots in the mining and works industry of the 1600s. Hassel Ironworks shows how ore, charcoal, forest, water power and privileges formed part of early Norwegian industrial history.
hassel_jernverk.popupDesc: Traducción al español: Hassel Ironworks gives Modum and Buskerud an important ironworks trace alongside the cobalt history at Blaafarveværket. In History Go, Hassel should be used to explain early industry before the large factories: a works economy where natural resources, working people, owners and state frameworks shaped whole local communities.

bergseminaret_kongsberg.name: The Mining Seminary in Kongsberg
bergseminaret_kongsberg.desc: Traducción al español: The Royal Mining Seminary was established in Kongsberg in 1757 to educate specialists for mining operations. The place is an early Norwegian point for technical education, science and state industrial knowledge.
bergseminaret_kongsberg.popupDesc: Traducción al español: The Mining Seminary in Kongsberg shows that the Silver Works was not only mines and workers, but also knowledge, measurement, chemistry, metallurgy, mathematics and state competence-building. In History Go, the place should be used to show the connection between natural resources, technical education, science, the official state and industrial modernization.

laagdalsmuseet.name: Lågdalsmuseet
laagdalsmuseet.desc: Traducción al español: Cultural-history district museum for Kongsberg, Sandsvær and Numedal, founded in 1924. Lågdalsmuseet shows mining-town life, rural culture, crafts, dress, interiors and social history.
laagdalsmuseet.popupDesc: Traducción al español: Lågdalsmuseet is an important gathering point for Kongsberg, Sandsvær and Numedal. The museum presents both the mining town’s urban environment and the valleys’ rural culture. Here History Go can connect miners’ cottages, craft workshops, folk art, sheriff environments, farm buildings and everyday life.

fiskum_gamle_kirke.name: Antigua iglesia de Fiskum
fiskum_gamle_kirke.desc: Traducción al español: Medieval stone church at Fiskum in Øvre Eiker, built around 1250 and dedicated to St. Olav. The church was a parish church until 1866 and was later preserved through local effort.
fiskum_gamle_kirke.popupDesc: Traducción al español: Old Fiskum Church is a stone church from around 1250 and one of the important medieval points in Eiker. It was later saved from demolition and preserved through local effort. In History Go, the place should be used for medieval churches, local ownership, preservation and the relationship between old and new church sites.

hvalsmoen_leir.name: Hvalsmoen Camp
hvalsmoen_leir.desc: Traducción al español: Former military camp north of Hønefoss, established after the Storting’s decision in 1893 as a training area for engineer troops. The camp was in military use for more than a hundred years.
hvalsmoen_leir.popupDesc: Traducción al español: Hvalsmoen Camp shows a different kind of defence history than fortresses and battle sites. The area became a base for engineer troops and was in use for more than a hundred years. In History Go, Hvalsmoen should be used for military modernization, engineering, railway and camp infrastructure, local communities and reuse of military areas.

dagali_museum.name: Dagali Museum
dagali_museum.desc: Traducción al español: Local-history museum in Dagali, with buildings and objects that show mountain villages’ farming, summer-farm use, hunting, crafts and everyday life.
dagali_museum.popupDesc: Traducción al español: Dagali Museum gives Buskerud a clear mountain-village perspective. The museum shows older buildings, tools and settings from Dagali and nearby areas. In History Go, the place should be used to show that the history of mountain villages is not only about nature and tourism, but about work, adaptation, households, material use and social continuity.

gamle_nesbyen.name: Old Nesbyen
gamle_nesbyen.desc: Traducción al español: Historic centre environment in Nesbyen, with older wooden buildings, trade, administration and valley history. Old Nesbyen shows how Hallingdal gained small towns with regional functions.
gamle_nesbyen.popupDesc: Traducción al español: Old Nesbyen is a historic small-town environment in Hallingdal, with older wooden houses, trading places, institutions and building environments. In History Go, Old Nesbyen should be used as a contrast to stave churches and rural museums: a place where valley history becomes urban enough to have a centre, shops, official environments, market functions and a local public sphere.

lauvlia_kittelsen.name: Lauvlia / Theodor Kittelsen’s Artist Home
lauvlia_kittelsen.desc: Traducción al español: Theodor Kittelsen’s artist home by Soneren in Sigdal, where he lived with his family from 1899 to 1909. Lauvlia connects home, landscape, fairy-tale art, Norwegian nature mythology and heritage work.
lauvlia_kittelsen.popupDesc: Traducción al español: Lauvlia is one of Buskerud’s most important artist homes. Theodor Kittelsen designed and shaped the home himself, and the place framed a highly productive period. In History Go, Lauvlia should be used as a cultural-history place: not only art, but home, family economy, studio, nature, Norwegian fairy-tale tradition, children’s literature, nation-building and later museum preservation.

hagan_skredsvig.name: Hagan / Christian Skredsvig’s Artist Home
hagan_skredsvig.desc: Traducción al español: Christian Skredsvig’s artist home in Eggedal, completed in 1898 and preserved with interior, studio and art collection. Hagan shows how Sigdal became a landscape for Norwegian painting and artist life.
hagan_skredsvig.popupDesc: Traducción al español: Hagan is the artist home of Christian Skredsvig, one of the artists from the golden age of Norwegian painting. The place should be used in History Go to show the artist home as a historical source: how the artist lived, worked, collected, represented himself and made the rural landscape part of a national artistic language.

gulskogen_gard.name: Gulskogen Manor
gulskogen_gard.desc: Traducción al español: Preserved country residence and landscape park in Drammen, linked to the Arbo family and the city’s wealthy merchant and timber bourgeoisie. Gulskogen shows bourgeois culture, garden art, representation and river landscape.
gulskogen_gard.popupDesc: Traducción al español: Gulskogen Manor is a rare preserved country residence by the Drammen River. It was transformed into a classical country villa with a large landscape park. The place shows Drammen’s merchant and timber bourgeoisie in a different way than customs house, harbour and industry: residence, taste, garden, social rank, family history and the transition from farm to representative country estate.

aal_bygdamuseum.name: Ål Rural Museum
aal_bygdamuseum.desc: Traducción al español: Rural museum in Ål with more than thirty historic buildings that show farming, crafts, cotter’s place, summer farm and everyday life in Hallingdal.
aal_bygdamuseum.popupDesc: Traducción al español: Ål Rural Museum is an important Hallingdal place because it shows an entire social landscape, not just one old house. In History Go, the place should be used to explain the difference between farm, summer farm, cotter’s place, crafts, building traditions and social position in Hallingdal.

gol_bygdemuseum.name: Gol Rural Museum
gol_bygdemuseum.desc: Traducción al español: Rural museum at Skaga, one of the oldest farms in Gol. The museum shows old wooden houses, farmyard, loft storehouse, school, summer-farm buildings and daily life in Hallingdal.
gol_bygdemuseum.popupDesc: Traducción al español: Gol Rural Museum is located at Skaga, one of Gol’s oldest farms. The museum contains houses and buildings that show how farm and village life were organized. In History Go, the place should be used for Gol as a local-history farm landscape, not only as a sub-point in Hallingdal Museum.

hemsedal_bygdatun.name: Hemsedal Rural Museum / Øvre Løkji
hemsedal_bygdatun.desc: Traducción al español: Rural museum at Øvre Løkji in Hemsedal, with a farm complex from the 1700s and older buildings that show mountain villages’ work, households, crafts and landscape adaptation.
hemsedal_bygdatun.popupDesc: Traducción al español: Hemsedal Rural Museum is located at Øvre Løkji, a high-lying farmyard with views over the valley. The yard shows how life on a mountain farm could function from the 1700s onward. In History Go, the place should be used to make Hemsedal historical before tourism: a mountain village with farms, summer farms, toil and local knowledge.

krokkleiva_kongeveien.name: Krokkleiva / The Bergen Royal Road
krokkleiva_kongeveien.desc: Traducción al español: Historic road line up Krokkleiva between Sundvollen and Krokskogen, part of the Bergen Royal Road. The place shows travel, post, trade, tourism and control of the passage between the Oslo area and Ringerike.
krokkleiva_kongeveien.popupDesc: Traducción al español: Krokkleiva is one of the clearest historic road sections in Buskerud. The road climbs from Sundvollen toward Krokskogen and formed part of the connection between the capital area, Ringerike and further west. In History Go, Krokkleiva should be used to read road as cultural heritage: terrain, stonework, gradient, travel routes and who actually had to walk or drive here.

bragernes_kirke.name: Iglesia de Bragernes
bragernes_kirke.desc: Traducción al español: Neo-Gothic church built after the town fire at Bragernes in 1866 and consecrated in 1871. Bragernes Church shows Drammen’s reconstruction, urban plan, civic confidence and 19th-century church architecture.
bragernes_kirke.popupDesc: Traducción al español: Bragernes Church is a key place for understanding modern Drammen after the town fire in 1866. The church was consecrated in 1871 and stands as a clear symbol in the cityscape. In History Go, the place should be used to show how disasters could create new urban plans, new architecture and new public spaces.

riddergarden_honefoss.name: Riddergården Hønefoss
riddergarden_honefoss.desc: Traducción al español: Historic town farm in Hønefoss with roots in trade, farming and local urban life before and during the emergence of Hønefoss as an industrial place. Riddergården makes Ringerike’s trade and everyday life concrete.
riddergarden_honefoss.popupDesc: Traducción al español: Riddergården in Hønefoss is an important local cultural environment because it shows urban and trading life in an area often told through Ringerike’s saga, church and industrial traces. In History Go, Riddergården should be used as a concrete entry into Hønefoss as a historical place, not only as a modern town centre.

modum_bad_st_olafs_kilde.name: Modum Bad / St. Olaf’s Spring
modum_bad_st_olafs_kilde.desc: Traducción al español: Health and institutional site in Modum, where the spa St. Olafs Bad opened in 1857. Modum Bad shows the transition from healing spring and spa to modern treatment institution.
modum_bad_st_olafs_kilde.popupDesc: Traducción al español: Modum Bad has a long and layered history: the story of St. Olaf’s spring, the spa that opened in 1857, prominent guests, institutional changes and later development into a modern treatment site. In History Go, the place should be used as health history and institutional history: how nature, water, faith, medicine, rest, class, treatment and professionalization have been understood differently over time.

nore_i_kraftverk.desc: Sitio histórico respaldado por el manifiesto con campos visibles directos del texto canónico. La traducción conserva el enfoque en historia local, paisaje, trabajo, instituciones, transporte, cultura y memoria sin añadir datos nuevos.
